transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm in the right place, and I really hope this doesn't sound too... silly. 

I'm just here because, well, I can't seem to stop focusing on my hairline. And the way my face looks—especially under those harsh lights at the restaurant where I host. I just feel like it makes me look so old and... strange. I mean, my coworkers are really nice, they always tell me they don't see what I'm talking about, but I just can't seem to shake it. 

Is that... does that make sense? I hope I'm not wasting your time with something like this.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking mirrors, trying to hide your hairline, or comparing your face to others?

Well, um... I guess I do have a bit of a routine. I mean, as a host, I really just want to look presentable for the guests, you know? It's important to make a good first impression. But... maybe I take it a bit far? I really hope it doesn't make me sound incredibly vain. 

Before a shift, I'll... I'll check the bathroom mirror. A lot, actually. And I try to comb my hair forward just a bit, just to sort of soften things up and cover it. I think it's normal to want to look nice for work, right? 

But then I start, um... well, it's a little embarrassing to admit, but I start taking pictures of myself on my phone from different angles. Just to see exactly what the customers will see when I walk up to them. I just get stuck replaying how they might look at me, and sometimes... well, sometimes I get so worked up doing all of this that I actually end up running late, or I'm almost too anxious to even go out front. I really try to be a good employee, I promise, I just get stuck in my head. 

Am I... is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Do you feel that the concern about your hairline or face is something that others cannot see or don’t understand, even though they may tell you otherwise?

Yes, um... exactly. Like I was saying earlier, I just can't seem to stop thinking about it. My hairline, and just the way my whole face looks under those bright restaurant lights... I just feel like I look so old and, I don't know, strange. 

And when my coworkers tell me they don't see what I'm talking about... well, they're really wonderful people, and I know they're probably just trying to be nice and make me feel better. I really appreciate them for that, I do. But... it's just so obvious to me. I don't want to say they're lying, because I know they mean well, but I just feel like they're humoring me, or maybe they just don't want to hurt my feelings. Because how could they not see it? 

I try to just smile and thank them so I don't seem difficult or, you know, too obsessed with myself. I hope that doesn't make me sound ungrateful for their support... am I explaining that okay?
How much does this concern about your hairline and face affect your ability to do your job or interact with others at work?

Well, um... I really try my best not to let it interfere, because I want to be a good team player. I take my job seriously. But... I guess it has been causing some problems lately. I’m a little ashamed to admit this, but I’ve actually been written up at the restaurant. It’s just that, like I mentioned, I get so caught up trying to fix my hair or checking how my face looks in the mirror that I end up being late. Or sometimes... sometimes I just miss shifts entirely because I just can't bring myself to walk out the door looking the way I do. I feel terrible about it, I really do. I hate letting my manager down. 

And with my coworkers... I try to be cheerful at work, but I've had to pull back from them. I've stopped participating in the staff photos. And they’re such a great group, they invite me to things outside of work—like gallery events, or they go on these group hikes—but I’ve stopped going to those, too. I just... I can’t handle being seen that way, especially out in the daylight or in pictures where I can't hide. 

I know I should just push through it, and I really am trying to be better. Does... does that answer your question? I hope you don't think I'm just being a careless employee.
Outside of work, does this concern about your hairline and face affect how you feel about yourself or influence what you do in your daily life?

Well, um... I really try to just live a normal life, you know? I want to be someone who goes out and enjoys things. But... I guess it does spill over a little bit. 

I mean, I still do my errands and everything, I'm not completely shut in. But... I do tend to avoid going out during the day if I don't have to. The sun is just... it's so bright, and it highlights everything I'm trying to hide. So I'll go to the grocery store late at night, or I'll just, um, I'll wear a hat if I absolutely have to go out. I hope that doesn't sound too strange. A lot of people wear hats, right? 

And as far as how I feel about myself... well, I try to stay positive. I really do. But it's hard. Sometimes I just look in the mirror at home and... I just feel so inadequate. Like I'm not good enough for anyone to want to be around me. I don't date anymore, and I've sort of lost touch with my friends outside of work because I just... I make excuses not to see them. I don't want them to have to look at me, or feel embarrassed to be seen with me. 

I know I shouldn't let it get to me this much, and I'm really trying to work on it. I just... I want to be a normal person who isn't so obsessed with his flaws. Is that... is that the kind of thing you were looking for? I hope I'm not sounding too pathetic...

Do you worry about your hairline and the way your face looks because you're afraid of gaining weight or becoming fat, or is it more about how you think your face and hairline look regardless of your weight?

Oh, um, no, it's not about my weight at all. I actually try to take pretty good care of myself in that department, you know? I eat right and try to stay active when I can. 

It's really just... it's just the hairline, and how my face looks. Like I was saying, it's the shape of it, the way the skin looks... it just feels so off to me, completely separate from anything to do with my weight. I don't worry about being fat or anything like that. 

I just... I want my face to look right, I want to look like myself again, not this... this version I see in the mirror. I hope that makes sense? I'm not trying to be difficult, it's just really specific to those things I mentioned. Did I answer that okay?
